The problem

Preferences live in texts.
Searches live in spreadsheets.

  • 01A client texts "actually, let's raise the budget" — it lands in a thread, not in the search that's supposed to use it.
  • 02By the time the agent re-types it into a CRM, a few listings have already gone out built on the old number.
  • 03General-purpose CRMs manage the deal that comes after an offer. Nothing owns the back-and-forth before there's a deal to manage.
What RealtorHelper is

One preference profile.
Both sides trust it.

Collaborative preferences

Agent and client edit the same profile. A lock decides who asks whom first — nobody's change gets silently overwritten.

AI Voice

Either side can just talk. A dictated note turns into structured preferences in seconds — no form to fill out first.

Live matches

Every edit instantly re-ranks what's worth a look, right where the agent is already working.

How it works

Nobody's change gets overwritten

Change an open field and it applies right away — the other side just gets a note to review it. Change a field the agent locked, and it becomes a suggestion waiting for a decision. Same profile, two views, always in sync.

The agent's view

One screen, not a tab per step

  • Four categories, one open at a time — Budget, Location, Property, Features.
  • Dictate or type a note — detected changes show up inline, field by field.
  • Approve or decline right on the field — no separate inbox to dig through.
The agent's view

Live matches, where the agent already looks

  • Every preference edit re-ranks the matches instantly — no search to run by hand.
  • New matches sit on the Board, next to Loved, To review and Passed — not off in their own tab.
  • One click — Add — moves a home from "worth a look" to the client's board.
The client's view

Looks the same, on purpose

  • Same categories, same AI Voice — on their own phone.
  • Always knows where a suggestion stands — sent, waiting, approved.
  • No results to sift through — just their preferences and what their agent's doing with them.
Why agents pay for it

What this replaces, and what it doesn't

Without it

  • Preferences scattered across texts, calls, and a CRM field nobody updates the same day
  • Clients who feel unheard when a showing misses something they already said
  • Agents retyping the same note into three places

With RealtorHelper

  • One profile, always current, both sides can see it change
  • A client who dictates a note and watches it turn into a real update
  • Fits beside the CRM agents already pay for — it owns the search, not the transaction
